replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Math and I have a tense relationship. I struggle with it, and it often stresses me out. Though I try, I often find myself lost in equations, which is frustrating since I prefer literature and biology.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Absolutely. Just the thought of complex equations makes me nervous. My high neuroticism means I overthink and worry about failing, which makes math even harder for me.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I tried an AI math tutor last semester. It was okay—I got quick answers, but it didn’t help me understand concepts deeply, and I still felt anxious during exams.
replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation as ax² + bx + c = 0. Then, calculate the discriminant (b²-4ac). If positive, use the quadratic formula: x = [-b ± √(b²-4ac)] / (2a). If negative, no real solutions. I often mess up the signs, though.

To find stationary points, take the derivative f’(x) and set it to zero. Solve for x, then plug those values back into f(x) to find the y-values. Check the second derivative to determine if they’re maxima or minima. I usually skip this step and just guess, which is not ideal.
